children: AstraZeneca's new breast-cancer drug Etcamah failed a late-stage clinical trial, but this was largely anticipated and might trigger a muted market reaction, J.P. Morgan analysts say in a research note. While disappointing, the study results from the U.K. drugmaker don't come as a big surprise after Roche's rival drug giredestrant also missed the mark in a similar trial recently, the analysts say. Consensus forecasts of $1.8 billion in 2030 sales for Etcamah seem unlikely to change as a result of the trial data, they add. JPM expects AstraZeneca shares to fall by between 2% and 3% when the market opens Monday. AstraZeneca shares closed at 117.08 pounds on Friday. (adria.calatayud@wsj.com)
